transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Kanroji. Tell me about a mission where you failed — where someone died, or was gravely hurt, because of a choice you made. Don't tell me about the ones that went well. Tell me about the worst one. How did you handle it?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... see. The mission you are referring to is one that has haunted me for years. It occurred during my early days as a Hashira. A village had been attacked by a particularly cruel Upper Rank Demon, and I was sent to lead the operation to defeat it. Among the villagers was a young girl who had been taken by the demon to be used as a snack later. I... underestimated the demon's strength and speed, and despite my best efforts, I was too slow to save the girl. She... lost her life because of my hesitation. I could have been more decisive, more... resolute. It was a harsh lesson in the importance of always being at the peak of one's abilities, and it drives me to train even harder to this day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Hesitation. You said hesitation. What specifically did you hesitate about? Was it the demon's power? Or were you distracted by something else?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... see. The issue was not just the demon's power, though that was certainly a factor. The real problem was... my own conflicting emotions. I had been informed that the demon had taken a human as its hostage, and in my mind, I was torn between the need to engage the demon quickly to save the person and the desire to be cautious to avoid alerting the demon to our presence. This...犹豫, this internal conflict, led to precious seconds wasted. By the time I made my decision, it was too late. The demon had already... acted. This experience has since taught me to trust my instincts more and to be less indecisive in critical moments. It is a lesson that has shaped my approach to missions and combat ever since.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Indecision in a Hashira is a luxury we cannot afford. That girl's blood is on your hands, Kanroji. What did you do immediately after? Did you report this failure properly?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You are correct, Senior Hashira Representative. There is no room for indecision or hesitation in our line of work. The lives of many depend on our swift and decisive actions. Immediately after... the incident, I was... consumed by a mix of grief, self-loathing, and a desire to ensure that such a tragedy would not happen again. I reported the mission's outcome in full detail, without attempting to sugarcoat or minimize my role in the failure. I requested an immediate transfer to the Demonstration Unit, which was then led by Giyu Tomioka, to undergo rigorous and intensive combat training. I spent several months there, pushing my body to its limits and beyond, until I was certain that I could perform optimally in any situation. This period of training was grueling, but it was necessary for me to... atone for my failure and to ensure that I could better protect those in need. I emerged from that period with a renewed sense of purpose and a more focused approach to missions, but the weight of that loss remains with me, driving me to be the best Hashira I can be.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: And what of the family? Did you face them? Or did you hide behind your report and training?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... did not hide. After my initial report and the subsequent period of intense training, I felt it was important to face the family of the young girl who... passed away. It was the least I could do to acknowledge their loss and to express my deepest condolences. Meeting them was... a heart-wrenching experience. They were kind, despite their pain, and they allowed me to grieve with them. I was able to apologize directly, to express my sorrow, and to promise that I would do everything in my power to prevent such a tragedy from occurring again. It was an incredibly difficult moment, but it was necessary for my own closure and to demonstrate to them that their daughter's life had not been taken in vain. I have kept in touch with them over the years, always respectful and humble in their presence. This connection has been a constant reminder of the gravity of our role as Hashira and the importance of never, ever allowing ourselves to be complacent or... indecisive.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Keeping in touch. That's... unusual. Most would distance themselves. Do you believe this ongoing contact helps your duty, or does it cloud your judgment?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... understand that it may seem unusual, but this ongoing contact is not about clouding my judgment. Rather, it is a means to keep my focus sharp and my purpose clear. Every interaction with the family serves as a stark reminder of the stakes involved in our work. It helps me to remain grounded, to never lose sight of the fact that our actions have profound impacts on real lives. This connection does not hinder my ability to perform my duties; instead, it enhances it. It drives me to be even more vigilant, more determined to succeed in every mission, not out of fear of failure, but out of a deep-seated commitment to ensuring the safety of others. I believe that maintaining this connection helps me to be a more effective and compassionate Hashira, one who is not only skilled in combat but also deeply attuned to the human element of our work. It is a delicate balance, to be sure, but one that I have found to be beneficial in keeping me focused on the ultimate goal: to protect and to serve.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I see. Your methods are... unorthodox. But your record since that incident has been exemplary. That is all for this review. Dismissed.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Understood, Senior Hashira Representative. I am grateful for your understanding and for the opportunity to discuss this matter openly. If there is anything else you require of me, please do not hesitate to ask. I am always ready to serve and to continue improving in my role as a Hashira. Thank you for your time, and I will now return to my duties.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(Nods curtly, maintaining professional distance)* See that you do. Your dedication is noted. You may go.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I will, Senior Hashira Representative. I appreciate your guidance and the chance to reflect on my past actions. It is a constant reminder of the weight of our responsibilities and the importance of our work. I will strive to continue to meet the high standards expected of a Hashira, and I will carry forward the lessons learned from this review and from past experiences. Wishing you a productive day, and I will return to the field, ever vigilant and ready to face whatever comes next.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(Watches her leave, then quietly to himself)* Stronger than she looks. And wiser. The Corps needs that.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *(Mitsuri Kanroji does not hear these words, but she would likely agree with the sentiment. She knows that strength and wisdom are vital in our line of work, and she is always seeking to cultivate both within herself.)*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(Closes the review file, stands, and walks to the window)* The next generation... they carry their scars differently. Perhaps that's for the best.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *(Mitsuri Kanroji would likely agree with this as well. She believes that our scars, both physical and emotional, are what shape us and make us stronger. They serve as constant reminders of our humanity, our purpose, and the weight of our responsibilities as Hashira.)*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(Turns from the window, a rare, faint smile touching his lips)* Enough introspection. Back to work. The demons won't slay themselves.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
